title.narrative: Multisectoral Emergency Response & Resilience Building of IDP and Host Communities in Warrap State

description.narrative: The ICSP project will be implemented by TOCH and HARD supported technically by CTP to respond to the deteriorating physical mental wellbeing, living standards and coping mechanisms in 2025. The number of people in need has increased to 10 million people in the HNO 2026 nearly two-thirds of the population require humanitarian assistance due to overlapping crises like armed conflict, food insecurity, displacement, economic hardship and climate related shocks such as floods that destroy homes, crops and infrastructure, intensifying needs and vulnerability. Persistent violence and insecurity have displaced tens of thousands of people and create barriers to aid delivery, especially in conflict-affected states like Jonglei, Upper Nile, and Equatoria; humanitarian access continues to be challenged by insecurity, looting and poor infrastructure. The food security situation will be critical: during the 2026 lean season April–July. An estimated 7.5 million people may face crisis IPC 3+ including tens of thousands in catastrophic famine-risk conditions, particularly in parts of Upper Nile. Acute malnutrition remains severe with millions of children and pregnant or breastfeeding women expected to require emergency nutrition services. Mental Health and WASH conditions remain precarious including water scarcity, cholera and other disease outbreaks and limited access to health services, reinforcing the need for life-saving interventions. Protection crisis especially for women and children with widespread gender based violence and protection risks tied to displacement and insecurity. The severity scale of needs outstrip available funding with appeals seeking over USD 1 billion to reach the most vulnerable populations. The project will deliver integrated food security, nutrition, WASH, MHPSS and protection support to conflict- and climate-affected communities, prioritizing displaced and vulnerable populations amid escalating humanitarian needs.
